name: Dig Tsho, Khumbu, Nepal (1985)

sources.citation: Vuichard, D. & Zimmermann, M. (1987), as reported in Bajracharya, Shrestha & Rajbhandari, 'Glacial Lake Outburst Floods in the Sagarmatha Region', Mountain Research and Development 27(4)
Cenderelli & Wohl-type peak discharge compilation, 'Peak discharge estimates of glacial-lake outburst floods and normal climatic floods in the Mount Everest region, Nepal'

sourced.crestElev: moraine dam was 60 m high at its lowest point just before breach (Vuichard & Zimmermann 1987, via Bajracharya et al. 2007)
sourced.initialWL: lake believed full to its rim just before the outbreak (Bajracharya et al. 2007) — modeled as level with crestElev
sourced.volumeM3: ~5,000,000 m3 of water released (Bajracharya et al. 2007)

unsourcedFieldsNote: No sourced geometry or moraine-till erodibility data found for this case yet. This trigger was a wave-induced overtopping (ice avalanche of ~150,000 m3 into the lake — see gen2d/gen3d for the wave-generation side of this event, not yet chained into this breach run). Treat this case as a seed/plausibility check only, not a validated result, until real geometry and till properties are sourced.

peakDischargeM3s.note: 1600 m3/s reported at/near the breach site (Vuichard & Zimmermann 1987, via Bajracharya et al. 2007). A separate compilation reports ~1375 m3/s at a gauge 7.1 km downstream — the two aren't directly comparable (different measurement points) but both are included as the genuine range across sources rather than picking one.
peakDischargeM3s.source: Vuichard & Zimmermann 1987; Cenderelli-type peak discharge compilation

breachFormationHours.note: No sourced breach-formation duration found yet for this event. Peak flow velocities of 4-5 m/s are reported (Vuichard & Zimmermann 1987) but that's a flow velocity downstream, not a breach-formation timescale — do not convert one into the other.
